inShort: A speeds up at B, and B counters with a short push and no backswing: first a block, then 30 % power, then 70–80 %.
rules: A and B stand at the kitchen line, straight across. A feeds firm balls at B's forehand side, from the body out to wide.
Round 1: B only blocks. Paddle out in front, elbow in front of the ribs, no backswing. 10 balls.
Round 2: B pushes through the ball by 15–30 cm at about 30 % power. 10 balls.
Round 3: the same short push at 70–80 % power. Set the paddle first, then accelerate. 10 balls.
tooEasy: B plays a high, dead dink, and A speeds it up without warning: 8 of 10 at B's forehand, 2 down B's line. B counts clean counters; 5 of 10 is a good score.
tooHard: B stays on round 2, and A feeds slower, always to the same spot.
goodLooksLike: B's counter goes back flat and low over the net, and B's paddle ends in front of the body, never behind it.

drill.title: Counter Window Progression (Block → Short Push → Power)
